newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil rejects U.S. charges over car rules.
newsitem.headline: Brazil rejects U.S. charges over car rules.

text.p: The Brazilian government on Tuesday rejected U.S. charges its car import rules were hurting U.S. exports but said it was willing to consult with Washington.

The Brazilian Foreign Ministry, reacting to a decision by Washington to start an investigation under so-called Section 301 U.S. trade law, said Brazil's car industry rules were a stimulus to U.S. car and car part exports.
It said the rules did not have any discriminatory impact on U.S. exports and noted that both Brasilia and the United States were willing to talk.

Jose Alfredo Graca Lima, head of the ministry's economics department, told Reuters Brazil considered the Section 301 investigation, which allows for retaliatory measures, an internal matter for Washington.
"But we obviously are not in concordance with the view that the (Brazilian car industry) regime affects in a negative way U.S. exports, to the contrary," Graca Lima said.
"I note there is no indisposition to consult (on the part of the Americans or of Brazil)," he added.
Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said the U.S. was challenging Brazil's tariffs because they affected the U.S. car industry. It was also challenging other countries.

The U.S. unilateral action runs parallel to formal consultations in the World Trade Organization. The rules allow manufacturers to import cars and parts at a preferential 35 percent tariff if they export in equal quantities from Brazil.
Graca Lima said WTO consultations requested by Japan, Korea and the European Union had all but fizzled out after Brazil introduced a quota-based low-tariff system for them.
